## 4e. The skip model, native (Nov 12; replaces turn 17's "distilled from W")

SIMON, Nov 12: "The model should be a skip model natively, with the number of steps to skip passed as input. Passing
1 results in the normal model. The output of the model is not the future state but a farther projection state 6
steps in the future such that computing the state 2 steps in the future is done by lerping the current state and the
future state with alpha 2/6. We can train it using the data directly. We can make it smoother around the
extremities of the valid range of desired skip sizes by training for skip sizes 0 and -1 by extrapolating the
prediction for size 1. We can also make it more consistent by training larger skip sizes on its own input with
size 1. [...] twins or drop masks to have estimates of uncertainties of the model to follow efficienttdmpc."

THE MODEL. One network, W itself: S(s, a, k) for k decisions ahead, K = 6 the largest (0.2 s at 30 decisions a
  second). It outputs a PROJECTION P - the state K decisions ahead if the motion went on at its average rate over
  the k decisions - and the state k ahead is the lerp:   s_k = s + (k / K) (P - s).
  WHAT THE LERP IS: a reparameterisation, not an assumption of straight motion - P depends on k, so any s_k is
  reachable. Its value is SCALE: P - s is K times the average rate over the k decisions, whose size hardly depends on
  k, where s_k - s grows with it. One output scale for every skip is what lets one network learn them all - the same
  reason shortcut models (Frans, Hafner, Levine, Abbeel 2024) output a velocity conditioned on the step size.
  k = 1 IS TODAY's W: s_1 = s + (1/K)(P - s) is a residual scaled by a constant. With k entering as (k - 1)/(K - 1),
  zero at k = 1, the k = 1 path is W's arithmetic exactly - its tests must hold unchanged (R7).
  THE ACTION OVER A SKIP: the target action HELD for the k decisions (the filter making the applied action smooth),
  as W takes one action for one decision. Held, the skip composes - S(S(s,a,i), a, j) is a skip of i + j under the
  same a - which the consistency loss needs and the planner's piecewise-constant offsets use. Not closed-loop under
  pi: that would make S move as pi trains, and W - the k = 1 case - must stay open-loop for pi's gradients.
  THE OTHER OUTPUTS, each with its own composition law, so consistency covers them too: the log-survival over the
  skip (adds: log P(i+j) = log P(i) + log P(j | i)) and the discounted reward along it (adds, the second part
  discounted by gamma^i). A planner judges the path, not only where it ends.

THE NUMBERS ARE TWEAKABLE (Simon, Nov 12: "Numbers will be tweakable. My intuition tells me that the best skip time
  will end up between 0.1 and 0.3 but we will experiment. The planner could make trajectories with short skip at the
  beginning and long at the end."). K and the skips trained are a run's options, never constants in code; the night's
  experiments set them, the expected best between 0.1 and 0.3 s (3 to 9 decisions at 30 a second). THE PLANNER's
  SCHEDULE: a candidate's skips short at its start, where the choice acts at once and must be precise, long at its
  end, where only the direction matters and the model's uncertainty has grown - one network serves every schedule,
  the skip being an input. The schedule is the planner's option too (turn 18).

THE LOSSES.
  L1 DATA, k = 1: every recorded transition - W's loss today, unchanged, weighted so SuperMimic's gradients keep
     the fine model's accuracy (watched: the k = 1 loss against a k = 1-only control, the smoke run's method).
  L2 DATA, k > 1: targets s_{t+k} from the same windows (a window of K + 1 records in one segment). Exact only where
     the action was held; ordinary records vary their action each decision. So: a share of worlds HOLD their target
     action for K decisions at a time (action repeat - also a known help to exploration), exact data for every k;
     other windows give k > 1 targets with their mean action, at a low weight.
  L3 CONSISTENCY - Simon's "larger skip sizes on its own input with size 1": the k-skip's target is the model's own
     composition, held action, stop-gradient (a slowly averaged copy of the weights as the target network):
     S(s,a,k)  ->  S(S(s,a,i), a, k - i). With i = 1 it is Simon's chain; with i = k/2 it is the shortcut models'
     halving, whose errors compound over log2 K compositions instead of K. Both, drawn at random. Where L2's data is
     approximate (an action not held), L3's target is exact for the conditioning - so L3 is the main k > 1 signal and
     L2 anchors it to the physics.
  L4 THE LOW END - Simon's k = 0 and k = -1, extrapolated from k = 1. At k = 0 the state is s whatever P is, so what
     is trained there is P's rate. ONE CORRECTION: extrapolating the k = 1 prediction at a constant rate (s_-1 = 2s -
     s_1) asks for zero acceleration at the boundary - a bias for a falling body. The extrapolation through s, s_1
     and s_2 (quadratic: s_-1 = 3s - 3s_1 + s_2) keeps the curvature. Its purpose is the k-input's smoothness where
     the trained range starts; it is kept only if a control shows it helps (its weight small, its gain measured).
     The high end needs no extrapolation: L3 at k = K + 1, composed of K and 1, trains it.
  THE UNCERTAINTY. TWINS: two networks, different seeds and their own window draws, the same kernels run twice -
     their disagreement d(s, a, k), as TD-MPC2 does for its values with an ensemble. Drop masks would need a mask
     in the kit's kernels; twins need nothing new, so twins first. AND A FREE ONE: the gap between a direct k-skip
     and its composition (L3's residual at use time) - where the model is incoherent it is usually wrong.
     USES: the planner's screening cost gains lambda * d - a planner otherwise finds the candidates where the model
     is optimistically wrong (exploitation of the model's errors; MOPO's and MOReL's pessimism answer it); the
     skip size chosen per candidate (coarse where d is small); and, measured before used, a share of starts drawn
     where d is large.

THE PIECES (each read before it is cut; each checked, and seen to fail):
  17a k AS INPUT, THE PROJECTION AS OUTPUT, in the kit's world model. CHECK: at k = 1 W's tests bit for bit (R7);
      the gradient through k and the lerp against zimrnum's. SEEN TO FAIL: the lerp's alpha as 1/k.
  17b L2 and the held-action worlds: the gather's targets k records on; a share of worlds holding their action.
      CHECK: the targets against the records by hand; held worlds' actions constant over their holds.
  17c L3, the consistency: composition, stop-gradient, the averaged target weights. CHECK: on held-out windows, the
      k > 1 loss with L3 below a control without it (the smoke run's method). SEEN TO FAIL: the target's gradient not
      stopped - the two sides collapse together (watched as the loss falling and the error to the data not).
  17d L4, the low end, quadratic. CHECK: its gain against a control; kept or dropped by that number.
  17e survival and reward over a skip, their composition laws in L3. CHECK: against sums over recorded windows.
  17f twins and their disagreement. CHECK: disagreement larger on held-out starts than on trained ones.
  ABOUT 8 SMALL TURNS where 4d had 2-3; turn 18 (T) then screens with S and its disagreement, turn 19 (F) as written.

## 4f. SuperMimic's policy trained through skips (Nov 12)

SIMON, Nov 12: "brainstorm and add to the plan the training of supermimic policies using trajectory made with
different skips. Some proportion with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 skips. Is that actually possible?"

TODAY: pi learns by backpropagation through W over a window - pi acts at every decision, W steps one decision, the
tracking loss against the reference at every decision, its gradient carried back through W into every action. A
window of 16 decisions sees half a second.

THROUGH THE NATIVE SKIP MODEL (4e): a rollout is a SCHEDULE of skips k_1, k_2, ... - at each node pi acts once from
the node's state, its action held for k decisions, S jumps k decisions ahead; the loss at each node against the
reference at that node's frame, weighted by k (the time it stands for) and discounted by gamma^k between nodes. The
gradient flows back through every jump into every node's action, exactly as through W. Mechanically nothing is new
but the skip's input and the schedule: the starts are recorded states, the targets are the reference tables.

WHAT IT GIVES:
  HORIZON. Twenty nodes of 6 decisions are 4 s; of 1, two thirds of a second. The policy is told what an action
     leads to seconds later - a fall, a lost balance, a way back - at the cost of twenty network calls, not 120.
     This is the termination problem's own horizon: the consequences that decide whether a character survives
     arrive later than a short window sees.
  BETTER-CONDITIONED GRADIENTS. Backpropagation through many steps of contact dynamics explodes or vanishes; a jump
     of 6 is one Jacobian where 6 steps are a product of 6. Fewer, smoother links carry a long horizon's gradient
     with less noise.

WHAT IT CHANGES - THE CATCH: at a node of k > 1 the action is held for k decisions, so what is optimised there is a
  policy whose action is good WITHOUT correction for k decisions. Deployed, pi corrects at every decision. Trained
  only so, pi would be conservative and imprecise; mixed in, it biases pi toward states from which even held actions
  survive - robust states, which may be welcome, but a bias all the same. THREE WAYS TO MEET IT, cheapest first:
  (1) SCHEDULES, NOT UNIFORM SKIPS: short nodes first, long ones after - 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 6, ... The first nodes
      train the control pi really exerts, at k = 1; the long tail is there for its gradient into those first
      actions - a differentiable look at the consequences, like a critic made of the model. The tail's own actions
      are judged under the hold, a bias confined to the tail. This matches the planner's schedule (short early, long
      later, Simon's word on 4e) - one notion of a plan for both.
  (2) THE TAIL's LOSS WEIGHTED DOWN, its weight an option, measured against (1) alone.
  (3) THE SKIP AS pi's INPUT (pi(s, goal, k)), deployed at k = 1: the held-action policy and the corrected one kept
      apart, sharing what they can. Costs an input and a question - does k > 1 training still help k = 1? - which a
      control answers.
  Simon's proportions (some windows of 1, of 2, ... of 6 throughout) are the uniform case, kept as an option and
  compared with the schedules: whole windows of 6 train pi only as a held-action policy.

OTHER CARE:
  THE GOAL AT A NODE. pi reads the reference one frame ahead; at a node of k, the reference k frames ahead is what
     its held action aims at. Which one pi reads there is a choice, measured; the loss is at the node's frame.
  THE MODEL's ERRORS, EXPLOITED. A policy optimised through a model finds where the model is optimistically wrong,
     more so over long horizons. 4e's twins give the disagreement along a rollout: added to the loss as a penalty, or
     cutting the rollout where it passes a bound. S's k > 1 accuracy, measured by 17c, bounds how long a tail is
     trusted.
  THE INTERMEDIATE STATES of a jump are the lerp's (4e), the model's own straight line; the loss is at the nodes,
     where S is trained, not along the lines between them.

WHAT THE KIT's TRAINING ACTUALLY REQUIRES (read Nov 12, Simon: "I was under the impression that the way the training
works demand uniform windows?"). The rollout is STEP-MAJOR: the kit lays out one block per step, every row of the
batch side by side in it, and runs the policy, then the world model, over all rows of step k before step k + 1
(`policyStep`, the blocks at `blockX(k)`). So EVERY ROW OF A BATCH RUNS THE SAME SEQUENCE OF STEPS - that is the
uniformity. It is across rows, not across steps: a schedule shared by the whole batch fits, each step's skip one
number for all its rows; different updates may draw different schedules (Simon's proportions become a draw per
update). What assumes one decision a step, and must change:
  (a) THE GOAL's FRAME. The gather takes step k's reference at the window's start row plus k (`lat_gather`:
      `start_row + step`). Under a schedule: plus the skips before step k, a per-step offset table.
  (b) THE ACTION FILTER. Between steps the kit blends the applied action toward the chosen one by the filter's share
      ONCE (`kit.filter`, `stiffness_filter`) - one decision's worth. Held for k decisions the blend is applied k
      times: the share becomes 1 - (1 - f)^k, per step, for the offsets and for the stiffnesses alike. Missed, a
      long node would move the applied action as if one decision had passed.
  (c) THE STEP's WEIGHT and DISCOUNT: the per-step weights the reward kernel already reads (`u_off + step`) carry k
      and gamma^(skips before), and the optimiser's horizon (`stepPolicy`: epsilon times the step count) becomes the
      weights' sum.
  (d) THE SKIP into the world model at each step - 4e's input - forward and in `policyBackward`.
NOT A CONSTRAINT: the policy reads recorded state only at a window's start; every later block's state is the
model's prediction, written over the gathered one. So a schedule spanning 120 decisions in 20 nodes still draws
windows of 21 records, not of 121 - the books' segments, cut by pushes every 90 decisions, allow it. (The world
model's own training is another matter: its targets ARE recorded windows, k records on - 4e's L2.)

THE PIECES (after 17, S native; each read before cut, each checked and seen to fail):
  17g pi's ROLLOUT THROUGH A SCHEDULE of skips: the node's state, pi's action, S's jump, the loss at the node's frame,
      weighted and discounted. CHECK: an all-ones schedule is today's rollout, bit for bit (R7); the gradient
      through a jump against zimrnum's. SEEN TO FAIL: the node's frame one skip off.
  17h THE SCHEDULES as run options - all ones; short-then-long; Simon's uniform proportions - and the tail's weight.
      CHECK (a control): on held-out starts, the true physics' tracking and survival of pi trained with a schedule
      against pi trained with ones only, the same updates and data. The schedule is kept by that number.
  17i THE DISAGREEMENT along a rollout as a penalty and as a bound. CHECK: against the same without it.
  About 4 small turns, and measurements a night may have to make (the tracking of a trained policy takes training).

## 4g. What the teacher's data trains, and when (Nov 13)

SIMON, Nov 13: "At training begin, the world model is bad. I am thinking we should train the policy only with the
winning executed planned trajectories. And we should train the world model with all the sim transitions generated
during planning. We should not use the world model at all during the first X minutes of training (maybe 30min?)" -
and on the answer: "I agree with all you said. Especially the fixed share for candidates to make sure the world
learns more from winners."

REPLACES, in O2 and 4c's e5-e6: the planned action recorded as the label on every planner decision either way
(DAgger's mixture), and pi's gradient through W from the first minute. Every number below is a run option.

G1 THE LABEL ONLY WHERE IT IS EXACT. A plan is open loop: drawn at its replan from the planner's state then, for
   the states that follow from executing it. Where it is executed, each decision's state is one the plan expected,
   and the plan's action there is the planner's answer. Where pi acts instead, the state drifts from the plan's after
   the first decision, and the plan's later actions answer states that never happen: a label there teaches pi a
   wrong action. So a planner's decision carries a label when
     - its planner follows its plan (`follows_plan`): every decision until the next replan; or
     - it is a replan's own decision (0 decisions since the replan), followed or not: the plan's first action is the
       planner's choice for exactly that state. This keeps DAgger's point - labels on the states pi itself reaches -
       at one decision in a replan interval, with no wrong label.
   DROPPED: the labels of a followed stretch whose planner lost its reference before the next replan - the plan
   failed (and F's anchor later is "planned trajectories that succeeded"). HOW, settled by reading the kit's gather
   (e5b4): a label and its flag in the record, and the distillation's sampler skipping a labelled record whose
   stretch reaches a loss (the books' `afterLossAt`).
   DECIDED ON READING THE KIT (Nov 13, 9b): A LABEL IS A FLAG, NOT A VALUE. Every planner EXECUTES its plan's action
   at its replan's own decision (`robotgpu.PlanFollowing.first_decision`), and at every decision after it only at
   the following share (`every_decision`). So every labelled record's own action is the planner's: the label is the
   record's action, flagged - no label column in every world's record (a fifth more ring for under 1% of the worlds),
   no second source for the loss; the distillation is behaviour cloning on flagged records, gathered by `lat_gather`
   as it is. Every replan yields a label (a non-followed replan's winner was otherwise used only as the next warm
   start), and DAgger's mixture allows the expert to act on some steps. THE COST: a share of 0 is no longer the loop
   without planners - the neutral setting is no planners (`planners` null); the beta-0 check is restated (9a/9b).

G2 pi IN TWO PHASES.
   PHASE 1, THE TEACHER ALONE: pi trained by distillation alone, `|pi(o, g) - planned|^2` on labelled records (G1).
     W trains from the first minute on its data (G3), but gives pi no gradient: SuperMimic's term through W is off.
     WHY: early, W's action response is wrong, and its gradient moves pi in arbitrary directions against a teacher
     that is right from the first minute.
   THE GATE: W's multi-step prediction error on held-out windows (D5's state error, rolled over W's training window),
     measured every few minutes, below a bar - the bar's value from the first runs. 10 minutes is the upper bound
     (G5; 30 until Nov 14): past it phase 2 begins whatever W's error, and the diagnostics say so.
   PHASE 2, RAMPED: SuperMimic's term through W ramped from 0 to its full weight over a few minutes; the
     distillation's weight fading as O2 had it (as pi's return on the planners' states nears the plans').
   THE LOSS, AS BUILT (9e, Nov 15): the action pi would GIVE - its raw output scaled, through the action filter's
     blend with the action given before, no exploration, no flow correction - against the label, the mean of their
     squared distance over every row and action number, times a weight (`LatentKit.labelBackward`,
     `zn_mlp.lat_label_bwd`). A label is an action the physics was given, so pi's side goes through the same blend.
     One decision, gathered as a one-step window from a labelled record; nothing rolled, W not read.
   DECIDED FOR 9f (Nov 15; Simon: "I agree with you"): pi's UPDATES BY KIND, as W's batches are (9d) - each policy
     update a label step (`policyLabelTrainStep`: its own Adam step, epsilon unscaled) or a rollout step
     (`policyTrainStep`), at a share. Phase 1 is every update a label step; the ramp is the rollout kind's share
     rising; the fading is the label kind's share falling. One mechanism for G5's shares of the compute; no two
     gradients summed in one step. The two kinds share Adam's moments, so the labels' gradient has a weight
     (`label_weight`) to set beside the rollout's (D3 logs each kind's loss; the gradients' lengths with the clipped
     optimiser).

G3 W's DATA: THE CANDIDATES' LOOKAHEADS, AT A FIXED SHARE.
   RECORDED: each candidate's lookahead, a stretch of its own in the books - from its copy to the lookahead's end.
     At O2's sizes (16 candidates, H = 8, a replan every 4 decisions) a planner makes 32 candidate decisions for each
     of its own: many actions from the same real state, the ACTION RESPONSE W's gradient needs - O3's question,
     answered by data the planner already makes. Discarded until 9c (`record_rows` skipped candidates); kept since.
   THE FIXED SHARE: W's batch drawn by kind at set shares, never in proportion to the data, which the candidates
     would swamp: the characters' own records (pi's worlds, and the planners' - the executed winners among them),
     and the candidates' at a fixed share - most of W's batches in phase 1 (G5), a quarter in phase 2. Whole batches
     by kind, not rows (9d): the critic trains on W's gathered windows and must not see the candidates'.
   THE WINNERS FAVOURED within the candidates' share: half of it from each replan's best quarter by score (the scores
     are read back already), the rest from all - so W learns most where the plans go, and still sees the losers'
     falls.
   THE WINDOW: a W window drawn from a candidate's lookahead fits inside it - W's window at most H decisions, gathered
     for W's window alone however long pi's horizon (9d). A run with a longer W window draws no candidate windows,
     and counts the batches refused (`candidate_batches_refused`).
   COST: 32 planners x 16 candidates x 8 decisions a replan, a replan every 4 decisions - 1,024 candidate records a
     decision, as many as 1,024 policy worlds make. The ring sized for it; the record copy one more block.
   HOW, settled by reading: `record_rows` run for the candidates at each lookahead decision; the copy of their block
     into the ring; the LOOKAHEAD AS THE RING's UNIT (9d: lookahead L's decision d at step L (H + 1) + d, the ring a
     whole number of lookaheads) - books were kept at 9c and dropped at 9d, the structure telling all they told.

G4 BUILT ALREADY, AND KEPT: the following share (beta, `plan_following_share`), `follow_plans` and `Sim.followPlans`,
   the replan's step 5, a new episode clearing `follows_plan`. Under G1 the share decides how many planner decisions
   carry labels and how many are pi's own, labelled only at the replan.

G5 THE PHASES' SHARES OF THE COMPUTE (Nov 14). SIMON: "For the first 10 min of training we should focus 80% of the
   compute on learning the world model as quickly as possible, using all candidates data, maybe with a bias to train a
   bit more on the winner. And only 10% on the policy dagger towards the winning plans. An other 10% getting
   trajectories from the bad policy to learn the world model a bit wider. But no using the model at first. Then as
   soon as the world is good enough we should spend half of the time on world and supertrack policy and half on
   planning in offset space around policy to learn the flowdpg residual."
   PHASE 1, at most 10 minutes, W's gate ending it sooner (G2):
     ~80%  W: the teacher's lookaheads (the candidates' physics) and W's updates - most of W's batches the
           candidates' (G3), the winners favoured within them
     ~10%  pi's distillation toward the executed plans (G1)
     ~10%  the policy's own worlds, whose records widen W's states: the rest of W's batches
     W gives nothing to anyone: no gradient through it, no planning with it.
   PHASE 2, from W's gate:
     ~50%  W, and pi's SuperMimic update through it (G2's ramp)
     ~50%  planning in OFFSET space around pi - a candidate's action pi's own plus its plan's offset - and F's FlowDPG
           update on the planned offsets (4d's 18-19)
     MADE PRECISE Nov 15 (4h's H4): the planning of phase 2 is in the MODEL - EfficientTDMPC's search around pi, on a
     share of live worlds and on replay states; the physics teacher plans only for the worlds in most trouble, within
     about 10% of the physics (about 80% in phase 1).
   THE LEVERS, as shares of a round's time (6b; D1 and D8 measure them): the replan interval and the candidates per
     planner (the teacher's physics), the worlds that are no planners (the policy's own records), W's and pi's updates
     a round, W's batches by kind (9d). At O2's sizes a replan every decision puts the candidates at ~80% of the
     physics (4,096 candidate decisions to 1,024 characters'), every 4 decisions at ~50%.
   WHAT PHASE 2 NEEDS THAT PHASE 1 DOES NOT: pi acting inside a lookahead - the candidates' rows in the kit's acting at
     every lookahead decision - so a plan can be offsets around it. Phase 1's plans are whole actions, since a bad
     policy is no anchor; the switch to offsets is the planner's change between the phases.

THE ORDER, replacing 4d's step 9 (rules R1-R7 unchanged):
   9a  e5b3c  the beta-0 check: the loop with planners at share 0 against the loop without, to the bit    1
              (restated in 9b: every world that is no planner, and its records, against the loop without)
   9b  e5b4   the label where it is exact, and its flag, in the record (G1)                               1-2
   9c  e5b5   the candidates' lookaheads recorded, their stretches in the books (G3)                      2
   9d  e5b6   W's batch by kind: the candidates' fixed share, the winners favoured (G3)                   1-2
   9e  e6     pi's distillation on labelled records, the failed stretches skipped (G1); its gradient     2
              against zimrnum's on a fixed batch. In two: the kit's label step and its gradient (done
              Nov 15); then the labels' books - a label kept once its stretch ends well - and the
              trainer's label update (done Nov 15)
   9f  e7     the policy's updates by kind (G2); the two phases: phase 1 pi's update the labels' alone,   2
              to the bit (R7); the gate on W's state error and its action response (4h's H3), the 10-minute
              bound, the ramp (G2). In two: the updates by kind, the phases, the bound and the ramp (done
              Nov 15); then the gate's measurements and their log
   Then 4h's order (Nov 15): the variants, the first run, the whole loop, then 17 (S).

## 4h. The goal restated, and the plan aligned with it (Nov 15)

SIMON, Nov 15: "Our goal is to use ideas from mppi, efficienttdmpc, and flowdpg as smartly as possible to beat
supermimic. We dont beat them on number of hours of mocap but we beat them on training time, quality, and robustness
and fluid return from very large perturbation. But we train only on a small mocap corpus of just a couple minutes. I
am thinking we could mirror and timescale dynamically the anim to augment our data. Find a good way to add that in
the plan. At training begin we can use mppi to kickstart the policy with dagger, but we must really focus on learning
the world as quickly as possible. Then as soon as the world is good enough we should dramatically reduce how much
mppi and focus on supermimic plus a flowdpg residual added to the policy trained with efficienttdmpc on skipmodel in
offset space around policy." The tree and this plan were reviewed against it; eight questions were asked, and every
answer was the recommended one - the decisions below (H1-H6). H7 holds the ideas this review added unasked.

THE REVIEW - what fits the goal already, and what did not:
  FITS: phase 1 as 4g and G5 have it - the teacher's lookaheads feed W at about 80% of the compute, the labels
    kickstart pi (DAgger's states: every replan's own decision), W gives nothing to anyone until its gate. The parts
    of phase 2 exist in the learner: EfficientTDMPC's search around the policy (`TrackingPlanner` over `KitMppi`,
    the mean-over-depths objective, the critic past the plan) and the flow residual with its FlowDPG and planner
    teachers (`FlowActor`).
  DID NOT FIT, each answered below:
    (1) Phase 2 kept much physics planning: C19's tenth of the worlds, each refining three candidates every
        decision, is about two thirds of the physics. (H4)
    (2) The physics is the scarce resource: 8,010 world-decisions a second on the RTX 5070 at 1,024 worlds (W1) -
        about 5 million transitions in phase 1's ten minutes. What can be learned from models and replay should not
        be bought with more physics. (H4)
    (3) W is dense tanh; SuperMimic's form (C12: SiLU, LayerNorm, a zero output, rounds alone) was scheduled after
        the first measurements. (H5)
    (4) The model planner and the flow residual are not wired to the device path: acting on the device runs the
        policy's three layers only (`LatentKit.actOnRows`). (H6)
    (5) No learner has been measured on Simon's machine; by 4d's order the first measurement was about twenty turns
        away. (H5)
    (6) The gate read W's state error alone. The policy's gradient rides on W's ACTION RESPONSE, which parted from the
        state error on Sep 24 (the response's cosine 0.43 on servo-plus-noise data, 0.20 on the teacher's
        recordings, for a model that predicted states well). (H3)
    (7) No augmentation - and Geno's two sides are not symmetric. Measured from geno.xml, each left body against its
        right partner mirrored across the sagittal plane (x = 0): the left forearm 4.3% longer (the Hand body's
        offset, 0.2596 against 0.2489 m), the clavicles 3.6%, rest frames up to 11 degrees apart (the hands); the
        legs' lengths within 0.3%, their rest frames within 7 degrees (the feet). A mirrored REFERENCE is a motion
        Geno can be asked to track; a mirrored RECORD is not Geno's physics. (H2)
    (8) Night 1's goal named no get-ups, while the goal says very large perturbations. (H6)

H1 WHAT BEATING SUPERMIMIC MEANS, AND HOW IT IS MEASURED (decided: against our own SuperMimic control).
   Not on hours of mocap - ours is a couple of minutes (`one_minute`: the dance, the get-up, walking, running).
   THE CONTROL: our reproduction of SuperMimic on the same clips, the same GPU and the same minutes - W in SuperMimic's
     form (C12), rounds of W alone first, pi by backpropagation through W with the critic past the horizon - and
     nothing of ours: no teacher, no labels, no variants, no skip model, no flow residual. CHANGED Nov 16 (4i): no
     rounds of W alone (I4: the official code has none); the second run's R0 the official's in every respect I9 lists;
     (a) the active time to I3's success, (b) with BlinkMimic's quality columns.
   FIVE NUMBERS, at equal minutes, ON THE ORIGINAL CLIPS ONLY (the variants are training data):
     (a) TRAINING TIME: the minutes to a tracking bar - the mean normalised return above the servo's on every clip
         (O1's L3 bar);
     (b) QUALITY: the tracking error per clip, its mean and its 90th percentile (the judge's);
     (c) ROBUSTNESS: the return rate under standard pushes - fixed speeds at fixed phases (the fixed evaluation),
         1 to 5 m/s, the recovery probes' speeds and the top the training's pushes reach (H8);
     (d) RETURN: from hard starts (starts in trouble), the return rate and the time to return;
     (e) FLUID: during returns, the action rate and the root's jerk - a return that snaps back scores worse than one
         that flows (Simon's "fluid return"; added by this review to the four the question named).
         [BUILT Nov 17, night: the recovery probe's `RecoveryBand.return_action_rate_sum`, `return_jerk_sum` over
         `return_fluid_steps` - each return's decisions from its loss, two decisions past the push, the means
         `meanReturnActionRate` (action units a second) and `meanReturnJerk` (m/s^3); in `recovery.csv` and the
         trainer's report. The action is the policy's as given, before the fleet's filter.]
   WHERE: the CPU judge and its probes are the device physics' twin (gate G1), so the evaluation runs as `judge.csv`
     and `recovery.csv` do today, on the weights the device trained (the trainer's host mirror); (e) is added to the
     recovery probes. An evaluation on the device only if the judge's time is ever what limits a run.

H2 THE VARIANTS: MIRRORED, AND REPLAYED ALONG SPEED CURVES (decided: variants as extra clips).
   Built once, on the host, when a run starts. Each variant is one more clip - its own tables (the simulator's
   `ClipPoses`, the learner's `clip_rows`), its own curriculum bins, its share of the starts - so nothing in the
   physics, the judgement, the observation or the learners changes: they read a clip as they read any clip.
   EVIDENCE that both help a tracker: left-right mirroring doubles a tracker's motions (RoboStriker, arXiv 2601.22517:
   14 minutes of boxing, mirrored); time-warping - accelerating and decelerating every sequence - for robustness to
   the motion's speed (Humanoid-GPT, arXiv 2606.03985: their corpus made about five times larger). Ours varies the
   speed ALONG each clip (Simon's "dynamically"), not one factor a clip.
   MIRRORED IN THE CAPTURE's SPACE, BEFORE THE COPY. Geno is built from the capture's own skeleton, so retargeting is
     a copy (`robot_geno.copyClip`, R7) - and that skeleton's two sides differ (review 7). So a frame is mirrored
     where it is still the capture's: every joint's world turn and place reflected across the sagittal plane, left
     and right swapped, and each joint's local turn recovered through ITS OWN rest frame with one fixed correction per
     joint - the turn that takes its rest bone onto its partner's mirrored rest bone - so a mirrored limb points where
     its partner pointed, mirrored, although its bones are 4% longer and its rest frame 11 degrees off. (Any vertical
     plane gives the same motion up to a heading, and the features are heading-relative.) Then copied, smoothed and
     grounded as every clip is.
     CHECK: mirrored twice is the original, within a bar measured on the corpus; at every frame each bone points as
     its partner's mirrored (the same bar); the feet's lowest points are the partners' (the legs within 0.3%); the
     feasibility pass (d2), per bin, within its noise of the original's. SEEN TO FAIL: the per-joint correction left
     out - the hands then point up to 11 degrees off.
     AS BUILT (Nov 16, the capture's half): `robot_geno.CaptureMirror` + `mirrorCapture`. MEASURED: the 11 degrees
     were the hands' REST LOCAL TURNS (geno.xml's quats), which the mirror never reads - it mirrors the motion's own
     turns; what a bone's direction shows is the bones' rest geometry: the BVH offsets mirror within 3.45 degrees
     (forearm to hand; the legs within 0.01), and the hands' capsules lie 4.9 degrees off each other's mirror image.
     Uncorrected, the bones point up to 4.88 degrees off (the right hand); corrected, within 6.8e-6 rad. The bones
     are the MODEL's (`restBone`): toward the child body on the midline, else the only child body, else - the BVH has
     no fingers - the leaf's capsule, outward; a body's frame is its capture joint's, so the bone is the joint's.
     AS BUILT (Nov 16, the clip's half): `robot_geno.copyMirroredClip` (mirror, then `copyClip`). TWO CORRECTIONS
     to the text above, from the code: Geno's clips are copied, CUT and grounded - nothing smooths them on this path
     (`bakeCut`: `window`, then `restClipOnFloor`; `Clip.smoothed` is the flex2 retarget's) - and the mirrored clips
     are BAKED beside the originals, not built when a run starts: the trainer embeds baked clips and has no captures,
     so the capture's-space mirror can only run where the captures are (`examples/geno_ppo/{dance,getup,walk,run}
     _mirrored.zclip`, 1.45 MB, the same cuts; the speed curves are still a run's own, at its start).
     MEASURED on the four cuts, before the grounding: each body's axes its partner's reflected after its correction
     within 6.9e-6 rad; the legs' joints within 0.26 mm (the hips' offsets, 11.316 and 11.290 cm: the legs' bones are
     each other's lengths); the FEET's lowest points within 2.22 cm, not 0.3% - Geno's two feet do not sit alike about
     their ankles: in the foot's frame the left box lies 2.0 cm nearer the heel and 0.8 cm further down the shin than
     the right's mirrored, so a sole whose ankle retraces its partner's carries its own offset, most when pitched.
     That is the rig, not the mirror: no turn of the foot can move a box whose centre is 5.5 cm from one ankle and
     6.3 cm from the other onto it. The grounding then rests each frame on its own lowest point. Bars 2e-5 rad,
     0.5 mm, 2.5 cm. The feasibility pass (d2) per bin waits for d2.
     MADE SYMMETRIC (Nov 16, Simon: "Try to make geno symmetric"): the model every run uses is now
     `robot_geno.writeSymmetricModel` - the measured model's records (`modelRecords`, the writer split into records
     and `writeRecords`, byte-equal for the measured model) with each pair the mean of the two read through the mirror
     (`symmetrizeRecords`: places through the parent's correction, shapes, inertias through Cj^-1 (M I M) Cj, masses,
     the larger limit; midline bodies their own mirror image). Kept: the rest frames' turns (the capture's, which the
     copy reads) and the bones' directions (so the mirror read from it is the measured model's). COST, measured: at
     rest every body within 5.4 mm of the bind pose (the left hand), every shape within 1.21 cm of its fit (the left
     toe's box), 60.04 kg kept; the copy's residual against the recorded captures 7.3 mm (was 3.3: the stretch alone).
     ON IT the mirrored clip is the original's mirror image: places within 5.1e-6 m, soles within 2.0e-6 m (bars
     2e-5, 1e-5), turns 6.9e-6 rad.
   REPLAYED AT A STEADY SPEED (decided Nov 16, Simon: "keep the timescale variants simple: 20% up and down,
     uniformly. Even during flight" - replacing the speed curves first planned here). Two copies of every clip, the
     mirrored ones included: played 20% faster and 20% slower, one factor over the whole clip, flights and all. A
     copy's frame f, at the physics rate, shows the source at time f s dt, s = 1.2 or 0.8 (run options). A pose between
     two source frames by C14's interpolation, ONE definition (a clip read at fractional source times): linear for the
     root's place, a slerp for every quaternion; the velocities follow from consecutive frames, as every clip's do; each
     copy grounded as every clip is. The faster copy has 1/1.2 of its source's frames, the slower 1/0.8 - so the six
     variants hold (1 + 0.83 + 1.25) x 2 = 6.17 times the corpus's frames. A jump played faster falls at 1.44 g and a
     slower one at 0.64 g: accepted, for the simplicity. Built when a run starts, from the baked clips.
     CHECK: s = 1 is the original clip exactly (R7); s = 0.8's frames 0, 5, 10... are the source's frames 0, 4, 8...
     exactly, and s = 1.2's frames 0, 5, 10... its frames 0, 6, 12...; between them, every pose within the interpolation
     of its two source frames. SEEN TO FAIL: the slerp replaced by the nearer frame.
     AS BUILT (Nov 16): `robot_dance.interpolatePose` - the engine's own pose calculus, `differentiatePos` over one
     second then `integratePos` for the fraction: a place's line, a hinge's, a quaternion's arc (a turn about a fixed
     axis at a steady rate IS the slerp) - and `Clip.atSpeed` (a frame within 1e-4 of a source frame is that frame;
     residuals the larger of the two); `robot_geno.clipAtSpeed` grounds the copy (`restClipOnFloor`, the bake's 1 mm).
     MEASURED on flex2's baked get-up (a free root and hinges): s = 1 bit for bit; at 0.8 and 1.2 the counts
     floor((n - 1)/s) + 1 and every fifth frame its source frame bit for bit; between, the lines within 3.7e-7 and the
     arcs within 6.6e-7 rad of the exact source time's path (bars 2e-6). On Geno's minute and its mirror image: 22,192
     frames, 6.164 times the minute; the dip between two grounded frames 1.8 mm at most (bar 3 mm); every frame 1 mm
     above the floor or more.
   HOW MANY, a run option: mirrored or not, and the two speeds beside each - (1 + 2) x 2 = 6 variants of the corpus,
     6.17 times its frames.
     AS BUILT (Nov 16): `lab.ClipVariants` in the run's task (`.task.variants = .{ .mirrored = true, .speed_change =
     0.2 }`; none by default; a speed change in [0, 0.5); variants are more clips, so SuperTrack's alone - PPO's
     refused by name), each clip's variants listed by `list` (the clip, then slower, faster; then the mirror image the
     same) and labelled ("dance mirrored at 1.2"). The trainer (`RunClips`): the motion's own clips first - the judged
     - then each one's variants: the mirror images embedded (four more baked clips), the speed copies built at the
     start (`geno.clipAtSpeed`, which now grounds a copy as its source rests: no frame below the source's lowest, the
     bake's 1 mm). The fleet holds them all, by character; the normaliser is measured over them all; the judge and
     the probes take the judged clips only, and the collapse alarm reads only theirs; the round's line gives each
     judged clip's time and the variants' together; `status.zon` lists every clip. The start line prints the device's
     binding limit, its memory and the activations' size, and the clips: how many, judged and variants, their frames.
     SMOKE (lavapipe, the portable trainer - the desktop one's 256 MB of activations is past lavapipe's 128 MB
     binding, refused loudly at the start): the minute with every variant - 24 clips, 4 judged and 20 variants,
     22,192 frames, 44% of the portable activations; four rounds; judged at round 1 and round 3, `judge.csv` naming
     dance, get-up, walk and run (and their "/whole" lines) and no variant.
   THE MEMORY (recounted Nov 16 from the code). Per frame at 60 Hz: the simulator's model arena 986 floats (99
     coordinates, 387 reference features - `localSize`, 24 bodies x 16 + 3 - and 500 reference-body numbers, 25 x 20)
     and the learner's tables 525 (the same 387 features + 138 joint targets, 23 balls x 6): 6.0 KB a frame, 21.8 MB a
     minute. TODAY's minute, six variants: 22,200 frames, 134 MB (88 simulator + 47 learner). FIVE MINUTES of mocap, six
     variants: 111,000 frames, 671 MB (438 + 233) - about 5% of the RTX 5070's 12 GB, the largest thing on the device but
     far from its size. Two arenas grow for it: `robotgpu_sizes.model_f` from 2^23 floats (32 MB) to 2^27 (512 MB;
     2^25 holds the minute), and the trainer's `acts_len` from 2^26 (256 MB, of which the tables would take 233) to
     2^27. One storage binding each: the trainer's start line prints the device's own per-binding limit and each
     arena's use, and a run asking for more variants than its arenas hold is refused by name. IF IT EVER MATTERS: the
     387 reference features are stored twice, the simulator's copy and the learner's (one shared copy: 172 MB of the
     671); the reference bodies' 20 numbers carry 6 of padding; or the speeds read on the fly, each world playing its
     clip at a fractional time - then a speed costs nothing and could be any. The web keeps the variants its memory
     holds (P5).
   THE VARIANTS' OWN RETURNS are logged apart - how far the policy carries what it learned - and never judged (H1).
   NOT DONE, ON PURPOSE: mirroring RECORDED transitions, or a mirror loss on the policy (pi(mirror o) = mirror pi(o))
     - both assume a symmetric body (review 7). The mirrored clips give pi and W symmetric experience through the
     simulator, honestly Geno's. RETIRED FOR W's BATCHES Nov 16 (4i's I15): Geno is symmetric now, so a mirrored
     record is Geno's physics; the mirror loss on the policy stays not done.
   SIZE: 3 turns - the mirror; the speed curves; the variants in a run (the arenas, the curriculum, the logs).

H3 PHASE 1's GATE: STATE ERROR AND ACTION RESPONSE (decided). Both measured every few minutes on lookaheads W has not
   trained on - the newest, read before any draw reaches them - and logged whether the gate is open or not, so the
   first run shows when other bars would have opened it:
   STATE: W rolled open-loop over a whole lookahead on the candidate's recorded actions against the recorded states -
     its error as a ratio to the no-change model's on the same windows (O1's rule: a bar is a ratio to a baseline).
   RESPONSE: two candidates of one replan start from exactly one state (the copy is whole, e1) and differ in their
     actions - O3's paired worlds, made already by every replan. The physics' response s'(c) - s'(c') against W's,
     W(s, a(c)) - W(s, a(c')), at the first decision and through the lookahead: their cosine and the ratio of their
     lengths, by feature group (the root, the joints, the velocities), and apart for planners in trouble.
   THE GATE OPENS when both pass their bars - run options, set from the first run, which logs both from its first
   minute. The 10-minute bound stays (G5).
   O3's PAIRED WORLDS ARE RETIRED as a block of their own (step f's f1 and f2): the candidates are the pairs. The
   response LOSS (O3's w_pair) stays possible on candidate pairs - built only if a run shows the response poor where
   the state error is good.
   SIZE: in 9f, which grows to 2 turns.
   AS BUILT (Nov 15): the measurement pooled over every state number, on the world model's own window from the
     lookahead's first decision. BY FEATURE GROUP: deferred - pooled, each group weighs by how much it moves (the
     velocities after one step, the pose by the window's last), so a group's own numbers come once a run shows the
     pooled ones hiding a poor group (the kernel takes a column range with a row stride). APART FOR PLANNERS IN
     TROUBLE: with H4, once the physics planners are chosen by their hazard.

H4 PHASE 2: THE PHYSICS TEACHER CUT TO TROUBLE, THE PLANNING MOVED INTO THE MODEL (decided).
   THE PHYSICS PLANNER (O2's MPPI teacher), after the gate: only the worlds in most trouble plan in the physics -
     chosen again at each replan by the planning hazard (`planningHazard`, `projectedHazard`: pushed, falling, lost),
     within a set share of the physics (10% by default, against about 80% in phase 1). It keeps giving verified
     recoveries - labels for pi, anchors for F - where the learned models are least right, and its lookaheads keep
     correcting W there.
   THE FUNNEL, IN TROUBLE (SkipWorld's; 4d's T): the physics planner's candidates are seeded by the model planner's
     elites, pi's action and F's samples beside the warm start - the physics refines what the model screened, for the
     physics of today's 16 candidates.
   THE MODEL PLANNER (EfficientTDMPC's search, `TrackingPlanner`), in OFFSET space around pi, through W first (a skip
     of 1) and through S once it exists; the mean over depths, the critic past the plan.
     ON LIVE WORLDS: a share of the worlds act on its plans' first offsets, so W is corrected on planned actions -
       where a model's errors hide (EfficientTDMPC).
     ON REPLAY STATES: EfficientTDMPC's reanalyze - replanned at an eighth of the acting budget, PESSIMISTIC: the mean
       over W's two heads less beta times their spread (beta 10, EfficientTDMPC's, which helps where episodes can
       end) - many more targets, for no physics.
   F, THE FLOWDPG RESIDUAL, learns from both planners: its anchor the offsets of plans that succeeded - the physics
     planner's in trouble, and the model planner's where the world that executed them kept or regained its reference;
     its correction W's gradient at its one-step estimate (its teacher 1). pi learns by SuperMimic's backpropagation
     through W, the labels fading (G2).
   THE SHARES stay G5's - about half W and pi's update through it, about half the planning around pi and F's update;
     the physics teacher's share is counted in the physics' budget, not the GPU's.
   SUPERSEDES C19's planner worlds (a tenth of all, plus those in trouble) and its physics refinement for every
     planner - kept for the worlds in trouble alone.

H5 THE FIRST RUN ON SIMON's MACHINE, RIGHT AFTER THE PHASES (decided). Three recipes of about 40 minutes, one after
   another (two hours): R0 THE CONTROL (H1); R1 THE PHASES - phase 1's teacher and labels, the gate, phase 2's
   SuperMimic update ramped in (no model planner, no F yet); R2 THE PHASES WITH THE VARIANTS (H2).
   IT MEASURES: the teacher alone against the servo on the dance from frame 0 (Sep 24, on the CPU: 17.05 s against
   6.65 s), at the run's start; the minutes to the gate and both of its numbers through phase 1; H1's five numbers
   for every recipe every 10 minutes.
   IT DECIDES: the gate's bars; whether the variants help at this budget; whether the teacher's start beats the
   control's - before the model planner and F are built on top.
   ITS PREPARATION, after 9f and H2 - about 9 turns (REPLACED Nov 16 by 4i's order, steps 1-5: c3' with I1, H8, O4
   with I3, I2, the recipes with I4, the smoke):
     C12  W in SuperMimic's form: LayerNorm from the kit's normed layers (`norm_fwd`, `norm_bwd`, `norm_params_bwd` -
          TD-MPC2's, on the device and checked already) and SiLU (two element kernels beside `mish_fwd` and

     O4   the critic's real returns: lambda-returns over each recorded window, so the critic is ready at the gate
          (H7a); and H1's fluid number in the recovery probes                                                       1
     the three recipes and the Windows build                                                                         1
     the three at five minutes here, on lavapipe at toy size, with O7's tripwires                                    1

H7 IDEAS ADDED BY THIS REVIEW, unasked - each small, each a run option:
   (a) THE CRITIC READY AT THE GATE. In phase 1 W gives nothing to anyone, so the critic fits real transitions only -
       one-step differences today. O4's lambda-returns over each recorded window, moved forward from step g into the
       first run's preparation, carry a fall's cost back through a window in one update, so phase 2's first
       backpropagation through W has a critic past its horizon worth reading.
   (b) THE FIVE NUMBERS' FIFTH, FLUID (H1e).
   (c) THE FUNNEL IN TROUBLE (H4) - 4d's T, kept for the worlds in trouble alone.
   (d) LATER, NOT BUILT: the reference's own clock. Speed-curved variants teach pi to track a reference played from
       0.8 to 1.25 times; gameplay will play animations at other time scales (Oct 18), and a return could slow its
       reference while it recovers (four-papers 10.2, re-anchoring the goal). For after night 1.

H8 THE PUSHES' RAMP: FROM THE FIRST MINUTE, TO 5 m/s BY THREE QUARTERS OF THE RUN, BRAKED BY THE RETURNS (decided
   Nov 15; Simon: "Are we ramping up the perturbation magnitude as training advances? We should plan for a gradual
   ramp up over 8 hours?" - his three answers: full at 6 h, braked; from minute 0, small; a top of 5 m/s).
   AS IT WAS: the CPU fleet's `Pushes` - none before `start_hours`, a straight line to full strength at `full_hours`,
     held after - ONE share scaling the push rate, the speed range above `speed_min`, and the starts in trouble (their
     share, their speed at the range's top). Night 1's recipes: none in hour 1, full at hour 7 - 0.5 pushes a second
     per character, 0.5 to 3.5 m/s, a quarter of starts in trouble. THE DEVICE PATH HAS NO SCHEDULE:
     `actTrainerOnDevice` passes `push_schedule_share = 1.0` at every decision - full strength from the first
     minute, on the path the first run takes. H5's 40-minute recipes planned no pushes, though H1's (c) and (d) score
     them.
   DECIDED:
     THE RATE at full from the first minute (0.5 a second per character), no longer scaled by the schedule: early
       pushes are small, not rare. With two minutes of mocap the pushes are what carries the characters off the
       reference: W meets those states before its gate (H3 measures only the trouble there is), and phase 1's
       teacher has trouble to label.
     THE TOP SPEED from `speed_min` (0.5 m/s) at minute 0, a straight line to 5 m/s - the recovery probes' top - at
       three quarters of the run (hour 6 of 8), then held: the rates' cosine over the 8 hours is at 17% of its start
       at hour 6, 7% at 7, 3% at 8, so the hardest pushes are met while the policy still learns. Each push's speed
       uniform between `speed_min` and the top; the starts in trouble at the top, their share opening with it.
     THE BRAKE - the top advances only while the characters still come back from pushes NEAR it. Evidence: OpenAI's
       automatic domain randomization (arXiv 1910.07113) widens a range only while the performance sampled at its
       boundary clears a threshold; Rudin et al. (CoRL 2021, arXiv 2109.11978) set each robot's terrain by its own
       success, a curriculum their massively parallel training needs no tuning for. OURS: the pushes in the top fifth
       of the range drawn; a world with one pending takes no other push until it settles - KEPT the reference, or
       RETURNED to it within the aftermath (`aftermath_steps`), against a loss that ends the episode or an aftermath
       run out; their kept-or-returned share over the last minute against a bar (0.6 to start - the first run sets
       it). At or above it the top advances along the clock's line, at up to twice its pace while behind it, never
       ahead of it; below it the top holds - it never retreats (ADR's lower bound is not taken: a top that falls
       would make the night's pushes depend on its worst minute).
     THE RUN's OWN CLOCK: full at three quarters of the run's planned length - hour 6 of a night of 8, minute 30 of
       H5's 40-minute recipes; the same rule for every recipe, so the control (H1) meets the same curriculum rule.
     BOTH PATHS: the CPU fleet's schedule and the device's decision clock (`DecisionClock.push_schedule_share`, from
       the top the host keeps - `actTrainerOnDevice`'s 1.0 gone); the device keeps each world's pending near-top
       push (its speed and decision) and settles it into counters the host reads each round, as it reads the
       trainer's decisions. The top's share is saved with the run's state.
     LOGGED, a minute: the top (share and m/s) beside the clock's line; the near-top pushes settled and their
       kept-or-returned share.
   SUPERSEDES: section 6's "from 1 h pushes, to full strength at 7 h", and night 1's push settings for every run from
     the first run on.
   SIZE: 2 turns, in H5's preparation - the rate apart from the schedule, the top's line and the brake on the CPU
     fleet with their checks; the device's pending pushes, its counters and the clock, with the twin's check.
   BUILT Nov 17 (the journal's entry has the checks), as decided, with these particulars:
     ONE RULE FOR BOTH PATHS in robot.zig: `PushBrake`, `PushTop` (`advanceTo`), `drawPush`, `settleWatchedPush`,
       `pushSpeed` - the fleet's step and the kernels `push_worlds` and `judge_episode` call the same functions.
     THE DEVICE KEEPS LESS than planned: one integer a world, the decisions left of its watched push
       (`watched_push_left`), and two flags a decision (`watched_push_settled`, `watched_push_came_back`). No
       dispatch and no readback added: the flags and the integer are in the worlds' integers the host reads each
       decision already. A push's speed is not kept either: every draw is a hash of the seed, the world and the
       decision's number, so the host makes a pushed world's draw again - which also gives a device run's log its
       pushes' mean speed, 0 until now.
     A PUSH IS WATCHED only for a world out of its start's grace and not in an aftermath; a start in trouble is not
       watched; a watch counts down only while the reference is held, and waits through an aftermath for the
       return or the episode's end; an episode cut short (the clip's end, the longest episode) drops its watch
       uncounted. A minute in which no watch ended advances.
     THE LINE's `full_hours` IS THE RECIPE's: 6 beside `rate_decay_hours = 8` in night 1's three recipes. Three
       quarters of the run is the recipe's to state, not derived - the one recipe (step 5) states both.
     CHOSEN WITHOUT A MEASUREMENT, for the first run to set: the bar 0.6 (as decided), and the WATCH's LENGTH,
       2 s of reference held - shorter than the probes' 3 s, long enough for a step and its recovery at 30
       decisions a second. `watched_pushes` and `watched_came_back` in the log are what to read them from.
     NOT TAKEN FROM ITS REFERENCES, as decided: the top never retreats (ADR narrows a range below its lower
       threshold; Rudin et al. demote a robot that fails).

## 4i. Speed, and SuperMimic's own code: InstantMimic, the official SuperMimic, BlinkMimic (Nov 16)

SIMON, Nov 16, after the two SuperMimic codes were studied: "Also read this paper carefully. Integrate some of these
ideas. We want to reap the benefits of this work, while still doing our offset flowdpg and efficienttdmpc and dynamic
stiffness action. Make the plan detailed and perfect and review it carefully." THE PAPER: InstantMimic (Choi, Leem,
Won; SIGGRAPH Asia 2026; arXiv 2609.09821), read whole. THE CODES: the official SuperMimic (`supermimic-main`) and
BlinkMimic (`blinkmimic-main`, built on InstantTrack's), read the same day.

THE SOURCES, AND WHAT EACH PROVES.
  INSTANTMIMIC, a systems paper: PPO motion tracking (DeepMimic's reward, PHC's observation) made GPU-native on MuJoCo
    Warp, then tuned by an LLM agent. MEASURED on an RTX 5090: an Isaac Lab tracking loop leaves the GPU stalled or
    underused 77% of each rollout step - the post-physics work (reward, resets, observation) 64% of the step, the
    physics phase 32%, the simulation itself 22.3%; outside the simulation the GPU busy 7.3% of the wall time. Two
    causes: many short kernels with the CPU's launch gaps between them, and CPU memory on the critical path - a state
    accessor copying from the CPU at every call (about 15.9% of the step stalled) and a reset behind an `.item()` (a
    full synchronisation every step). FIXED by the post-physics work as one kernel (a tracking reward: 281 us as
    PyTorch's many small kernels, 112 us under its JIT, 28.9 us replayed as a CUDA graph, 3.14 us as one Warp kernel),
    graph replay of the step and of PPO's update, the simulator's state read in place, the reset unconditional behind
    a mask on the device: the step from 14.88 to 3.03 ms, the physics from 32% of it to 91%; 0.613 million frames a
    second against Isaac Lab's 0.105 and mjlab's 0.157 (mjlab is MuJoCo Warp too). THEN THE SEARCH: an agent loop -
    plan, propose, experiment - one hyperparameter a cycle, its candidates trained with three seeds each and ranked by
    the median ACTIVE training time (wall time less the start, the checkpoints and the evaluations) to a success rate
    of 0.9 (whole clips completed by 32 deterministic worlds, judged every 5 iterations): a backflip from 18.77 s to
    2.17 s in 80 cycles, five independent searches ending between 2.03 and 2.45 s; five clips learned in 1.5 to 4.5 s
    each. ITS OWN LIMITATION (its section 7): ranked by time alone, the search kept changes that worsened tracking
    (cycle 21: the pose and end-effector errors up), the quality numbers being diagnostics only.
    FOR US: the profile and its fixes are measured, and they are the method this section takes; the search's choices
    are evidence for PPO on one clip, not for our learner - except where an input is an input (the root target, I7).
  THE OFFICIAL SUPERMIMIC, our reference for H1's control. Read for this section: the world model INTEGRATES
    (`MaxCoordRepresentation.apply_prediction`: per body a velocity change and an angular velocity change in the
    root's frame; the poses integrated; the root's world pose carried through the rollout as an auxiliary state); Muon
    on every hidden linear weight and Adam on the rest, both at 2e-4 (`build_optimizers`); the policy's goal ten
    future frames 0.1 s apart (`NUM_GOAL_FRAMES` 10, `GOAL_FRAME_STRIDE` 5 at 50 Hz), each the frame's joint positions
    and velocities and the anchor's rotation relative to the robot's - the relative POSITION goes to the world model
    only, because the deployed robot cannot measure it (`_goal_obs_group`'s comment); no rounds of the world model
    alone; its layers linear, layer norm, GELU (`nn.GELU()`: the exact one), PyTorch's default start, none zeroed.
  BLINKMIMIC: 40 LAFAN1 clips (2.45 h) to a normalised return of 0.82 with no clip failing in 3.4 min on an RTX 4090
    (3 seeds). ITS TABLE, iterations to a first 0.82: SuperMimic 7,898 (1 seed), SuperMimic with a policy average
    about 5,900 (3 seeds) - both ESTIMATED from InstantTrack's runs; InstantTrack v1.2 2,500 to 2,800 (its preset: the
    policy average, resets before recent failures, a contact reward, the world model 3 x 1,024, the rate 4e-4);
    BlinkMimic 1,200 to 1,500 (the integrating world model, half of its batches mirrored, Muon on the policy and the
    world model, the reference-action skip, resets aimed by the deployed policy's failures, a policy batch of 2,048 at

    average has its own line, and it is estimated. So a BlinkMimic change counts here where the official code or a
    measurement of ours agrees with it, and is otherwise a candidate for the search (I20).

WHERE WE STAND, read in the tree on Nov 16:
  THE PHYSICS: 8,010 world-decisions a second at 1,024 worlds on the RTX 5070 (W1), `newton_solve` 113 of a
    decision's 125 ms - the physics is already 90% of a decision, InstantMimic's after-state - but well below what
    MuJoCo Warp gives a humanoid of our size (InstantMimic's 0.613 million frames a second on a 5090; the models, the
    rates and the GPUs differ, so the ratio is a direction, not a number). `newton_solve` has MuJoCo Warp's shape, a
    workgroup per world, but runs its substitutions, mass products, line coefficients, measures and line search on
    the first lane alone, to keep robot.zig's order of operations (G1).
  THE DEVICE PATH's DECISION: `Sim.actTrainerOnDevice` reads EVERY world integer back at each decision and spins until
    they land (for the books' moments, the trainer's counts, the labels) - InstantMimic's `.item()`: the GPU drained
    once a decision, the next decision recorded only after. Its policy inputs, giving, recording, plan-following and
    resets are unbatched `run`s - a queue submission per dispatch - beside the decision's two batches. The replan
    reads its scores back and chooses on the host. W1 at 1,024 worlds: the flags read once at the end instead of at
    every decision, 8,272 against 8,010 world-decisions a second - 3% today, a larger share once the solver is faster.
  THE LEARNER: a round's updates are ONE recording, one submission, their numbers read back a round late
    (`syncMirror`, `refreshDeviceStats`) - InstantMimic's discipline already. Its dense layers are one thread per
    output summing from global memory (`dense_fwd`; zn_mlp's header names the tiled product as the later speed step);
    zimrnum's GPU kernels have a 16 x 16 tiled product (`zn_matmul.matmul_tiled`) the kit does not use.
  THE POLICY's INPUT: the state's features and ONE reference frame ahead (the reference's local features), each in
    its own root's frame. Where the reference's ROOT is, seen from the character's, is in no input - while the
    judgement loses the reference 0.6 m and 1.5 rad from it (`Termination`'s defaults) and SuperMimic's reward charges
    both (`superMimicTracking`'s root terms). After a hard push the character cannot see which way is back.
  THE BATCH: night 1's recipes take 32 windows an update (`rows`), W's and pi's alike - the official takes 4,096
    policy windows of 32 steps and 10 world-model batches of 2,048 windows of 8 a round (BlinkMimic 2,048 and 5). The
    rollout keeps every step's layer values for its backward (C12's note: four values per hidden unit per row per
    step in SuperMimic's form), beside the ring and the tables in one activations arena (2^26 floats on the desktop).
  THE WORLD MODEL: predicts the change of every feature (387 at Geno); the imagined cost is local
    (`lat_tracking_cost`: the features' squared distance, the head's and the tilt's hinges); nothing carries the
    root's world pose through a rollout.
  ALSO: no policy average (O6b planned, not built); Adam everywhere; no measured split of a round's time (D8 planned).
  ALREADY OURS, of InstantMimic's fixes: the resets by a mask on the device (C2); the simulator's state read in place
    by the kit, one device and two pipes (C3); the learner's numbers read a round late.

  I14 MUON ON W's AND pi's HIDDEN MATRICES (the official optimiser; BlinkMimic's too). The official `build_optimizers`:
     Muon on every linear weight between a network's first and last, `torch.optim.Muon(..., adjust_lr_fn=
     "match_rms_adamw")`, Adam on the rest, one rate (2e-4). Muon: the gradient's Nesterov momentum, normalised,
     orthogonalised by five Newton-Schulz rounds X <- aX + b(XX^T)X + c(XX^T)^2 X, (a, b, c) = (3.4445, -4.775,
     2.0315), the step scaled to AdamW's RMS (0.2 sqrt(max(rows, cols))). TO READ FIRST: torch.optim.Muon's source at
     the version the official requires - its momentum, its weight decay's default and form, its epsilon. The critic
     and F keep Adam (their references') unless a measurement says otherwise. COST: about 30 n^3 operations an n x n
     matrix an update - 3.2e10 at 1,024, 2.6e11 at 2,048 (a reason for our width) - on I13's tiles.
     CHECK: one step against zimrnum's f64 computation on a fixed gradient; the orthogonalised matrix's singular
     values printed (near 1, not at it: the coefficients trade exactness for speed); R7 for Adam's networks.
     SIZE: 3. NEEDS: I13.

the latent alone (the draft gave pi a small encoder beside the goal and called it the official's); positions advance
by the rate RELATIVE to the root's, and the frame change turns by the root's pose rate (the draft had the body's own
rate and the root's new velocity); the tiled kernels' results are the untiled ones' bits on the twin and within bars on
the device (a driver may contract a multiply-add differently in the two); the normalised return is checked on a run of
largest rewards, to rounding, not on a world held on its reference; I9 grew from 1 turn to 4 when the kit was found
to have no SuperMimic objective in imagination (`lat_tracking_cost` alone). ADDED BY THE REVIEW: I6 - checking I9's
sizes against the arena found night 1's recipes at 32 windows an update (`night1_full.zon`), against the official's
4,096; and R0's width set to the official's 2,048 (the draft had BlinkMimic's 1,024 there). LEFT OPEN, each its

THE ARCHITECTURE, AUDITED FOR FUSED KERNELS AND FEW TRANSFERS (Nov 17; Simon: "Make sure our architecture will allow
the benefits seen in recent work such as big fused kernels and minimal transfers with cpu"). Read in the tree, and
three pieces built the same day so that nothing new stands in the way.
  WHAT ALLOWS IT:
  (1) A PROGRAM IS DATA (`robotgpu_program.zig`: lists of a kernel and its invocation rule), and every kernel is
      `fn (invocation: u32) void` reading one uniform. So a FUSED kernel is an entry that calls several kernels'
      bodies for one world, each over its items - made at compile time from a program's list, the kernels untouched.
      Its limits: it is one invocation a world, so it takes only kernels that read their own world (not the copies,
      the curriculum's round, a planner's choice), it gives up the lanes across a world's items, and `newton_solve` -
      a workgroup a world, shared memory - cannot join one. So fusion is for the many small per-world dispatches
      (the observation, the judgement and the resets: 28 of a decision's about 110; the acting's 10), not the physics'
      wide kernels. STILL MEASURED FIRST (I1), as planned: on a GPU the cost fusion removes is the launch gaps, and
      (2) removes those without it.
      MEASURED ON THE 5070 (Nov 17, every dispatch timed): a small dispatch costs 13 to 17 microseconds, and all of
      a decision's small dispatches together - the observation, the judgement, the resets, the kinematics and the
      forces - are 1.5 ms at 64 worlds and 1.9 at 1,024: 5% and 1.5% of the decision. That is the most a fused
      kernel could save on this machine. Not built; the time is Newton's and the five per-world kernels' (I10).
  (2) A RECORDING (`Compute.beginRecording`): any dispatches of one pipe, each with its own copy of the parameters,
      as ONE submission - our form of a replayed graph. BUILT Nov 17: a batch inside a recording joins it, and
      `Sim.stepDecision` is one recording - the physics, the observation, the judgement, the resets; the acting's
      groups a batch each. MEASURED in the trainer on lavapipe: 4.0 simulator submissions a decision, from 29 by count
      (2 batches, 17 reset and observe dispatches, 7 inputs, 2 give, 1 record).
  (3) STATE STAYS ON THE DEVICE: resets by a mask (C2); the kit reads the simulator's state in place (C3); records
      enter the ring by a GPU copy; the learner's round is one recording, its numbers a round late. BUILT Nov 17: the
      start curriculum - its bins in the host's window, kept by a kernel, nothing read or uploaded.
  WHAT STILL CROSSES TO THE HOST EACH DECISION, and the item that removes it:
  (a) every world's integers read back, the host spinning until they land - the books' moments, the labels'
      following, the counts (I11). Nothing was added to it on Nov 17: the pushes and returns are counted from the
      flags it already reads.
  (b) THE TWO PIPES. The simulator's dispatches and the kit's cannot share a recording: each pipe has its own
      encoder and parameter table, and between them go three copies (inputs to the kit, actions back, records to the
      ring). So a decision is the simulator's 4 submissions and the kit's. I12's DESIGN, SETTLED HERE: a recording
      shared by a device's pipes - one encoder, each pipe's table uploaded before the one submission, the copies
      encoded in their place - then one submission a decision, and several decisions a submission once (a) is gone.
  (c) the replan's scores read back and its choice made on the host (I16).
  WHAT IS STILL COMPUTED FOR NOTHING (found Nov 17, with the teacher in the trainer):
  (d) THE CANDIDATES STEP THROUGH EVERY DECISION. A decision's programs run over every world, the candidates among
      them, though between two replans a candidate's state is read by nothing - the next replan copies its planner
      over it. Of a run of P planners x C candidates beside N characters that is P C / (N + P C) of every
      decision's work, on top of the lookaheads' (by count: a fifth at 64 x 16 beside 4,096). THE REMEDY, when I1
      shows it matters: a first world in the counts, so that a decision's programs start at the first character -
      the candidates are the batch's first worlds, and a lookahead already lowers the last
      (`Sim.runOverCandidates`).
      IT MATTERS ON THE 5070 (Nov 17): a world costs a decision 0.097 ms, so 512 candidates beside 1,024 characters
      add 50 ms to every decision's 121 - TO BUILD WITH THE RECIPE (the order's step 5), before the first run.
  WHAT COULD BLOCK, AND DOES NOT: kompute's eight arenas (what the worlds share fits the host's window); a
  recording's 2,048 parameter slots (a decision is about 110 dispatches; a full table flushes itself and goes on);
  the OS's GPU timeout (bounds how many decisions one recording holds: I12).


## 4j. The first night with more in it: the skip model, pi through skips, the search around pi (Nov 18)

SIMON, Nov 18: "Lets pick up the speed and have more features in even for the first night. We need to get the skip
model in. Revise the plan and proceed."

WHAT CHANGES. The first run is no longer "the system as built" (4i's step 5): it waits for the skip model (4e) and
for the policy trained through it (4f), and gains the two teacher pieces that make the physics planners OUR search -
offsets around pi (L1), chosen by trouble (L2) - and the flow residual on the device path (L4). With O7's tripwires
and the smoke, that is the night. The order after it (I10, I7, I5-I6-I8, I13-I14, I15-I20, I9, the second run) is
unchanged, minus what moved here.

THE SKIP MODEL's FORM, SETTLED BY SIMON (Nov 18, replacing the skip column built that morning): "We want the
model to have two outputs, the 1 step and the 4 step. The output is the projected state at 6 steps such that the
first head output is predict1 such that next state is lerp(s, predict1, 1/6) and skip head is predict4 such that
state at skip4 is lerp(s, predict4, 4/6). Having two heads make the net easier to learn. It is a bit of a velocity
model."
  ONE TRUNK, TWO HEADS: the dense world model's hidden layers, then two last layers - one-step and skip
  (`skip_steps` = 4) - each output the projection's offset P - z, the state `projection_steps` = K = 6 decisions on
  at the step's mean rate less the state. A step of k decisions reaches z + (k / K)(P - z). With the change in units
  of the typical change per decision the offset is K x (mean + spread x output), so a step adds k x (mean + spread x
  output) - and a one-decision step is SuperTrack's exactly (R7). Without the increments a one-decision step adds a
  sixth of its output: the same model, its last layer six times larger.
  ITS INPUTS OVER A STEP OF 4: the state at its start; the reference the servo aimed at during its last decision; THE
  MEAN GIVEN ACTION over its decisions - from the records directly (Simon, Nov 18: "we could train the skip head
  directly by giving averages of actions in the 4 step window instead of forcing actual worlds to have fixed 4 action
  blocks. We will lose precision but i feel like it will still work"). S2, the held-action worlds, is DROPPED from
  the night: the filter keeps four decisions' given actions close; the bias left - the policy's corrections within a
  step credited to their mean, worst in recoveries - is answered by S3's consistency under a held action, and
  measured: the skip head's error beside the one-step head chained over the same records, and split by how much the
  actions moved within the step. Held-action worlds come back as a small share only if that measure asks.
