- Nov 19 (I7 (4), FIRST PART: the root's math in zm, and its gradients). The root target and the root's integration
  must run in the kit's kernels (zn_mlp), which import zm and not robot.zig (robot.zig brings the profiler and the
  whole simulator into every build of the kernels). So the math moved into zimrmath's quaternion section, as generic
  rigid-pose math: `Pose` (robot.zig's, now with `numbers` and `fromNumbers` for robot.zig's `rootPoseNumbers` and
  `rootPoseOf`, and `pose_numbers`), `normalizeQuat`, `rotateQuatByAngularVel` and `twoAxis` (robot.zig re-exports
  all four), `poseSeenFrom` (robot.zig's `rootTarget`: the root target is the reference's root seen from the
  character's; robot.zig keeps `root_target_size` and its meaning) and `integratePose` (`integrateRoot`). One
  definition for the CPU, the simulator's kernels and, next, the kit's.
  NEW, THE BACKWARD: `PoseGradient` - the position's in world axes, the rotation's as a turn in the pose's own frame
  (three numbers, where the quaternion's four are tied); `poseSeenFromBackward` (the viewer's: g_pos = -R g_a,
  g_rot = g_a x a + g_x x x + g_y x y); `integratePoseBackward` (g_v = dt R'^T g_p, G = g_rot + v x g_v, the pose
  before's E G, g_w = dt J_r(w dt)^T G); `expRightJacobianTransposeTimes` (series below an angle of 1, closed form
  above). Checked against central differences of the functions themselves, not zimrnum's autodiff as the plan said:
  autodiff through the quaternion gives four tied numbers where the tangent's three are wanted, and differences on
  the real forward pass check the same thing.
  CHECKED: zm's pose tests (4: the worked root target, the circle, the backward against differences at a step's turn
  of 0.26 and 1.57 radians, the Jacobian against the exponential at five angles); SEEN TO FAIL, 7 mutations, each
  caught (the v x g_v term, the turn before, an axis's term, the position's sign, two series coefficients, the closed
  form's sign). The twin's policy inputs against the trainer's, the target on; the records test; robot's, robot_track's,
  the learner's and the lab's suites compile; lint, doc-gate, the pages. Two doc comments put back on their
  declarations (robot_track's `stateOf`, the kit's `barrierGrad`); robot.zig's position bridges named.
  TIME, this turn: about 4 minutes of builds and tests.
  NEXT: I7 (4), the gather's root blocks - the window's first root from its record, the goal roots from the table,
  wide row 0's slots exact - then the rollout's root step, then its backward.

- Nov 19 (I7 (4), SECOND PART: the root's blocks gathered, and the root moved through the acting rollout).
  THE GATHER (`lat_gather`, with `lat_root_target`): the goal's first seven threads of every step also write the
  root's two blocks, each [step][row][pose] - step 0 the window's first root from its first record, step k the
  reference's root at row k - 1's goal from the table; and the first row's slots get their exact target
  (`latFirstRootTarget`: both roots recorded, read from the ring and the table, not from a block another thread of
  the same dispatch writes). Later rows' slots stay zero for the rollout.
  THE ROLLOUT (`lat_root_step`, one thread a row, before the policy's turn at every decision k >= 1): the root at k
  from k - 1's, moved by state k's root velocity and angular velocity (robot_track's new `localVelocityColumn` and
  `localAngularColumn`; out of the normaliser's units) over the step's span of decisions (`skipAt` x a decision's
  seconds) - `zm.integratePose` - and row k's slots from it toward the goal's root. The kit's `imagined_root` holds
  the blocks, the two columns and a decision's seconds; the learner places them when `root_target` is on. The
  normaliser's offset now serves the barrier and the root. Params: a 32-byte group (the switch, the two blocks, the
  decision, the columns, the seconds).
  NOT YET: the backward - the slots' gradient is dropped (only the state's is taken), so the policy reads the
  imagined target but its loss reaches nothing through the root. The lab's refusal now says why: nothing in the
  policy's loss charges the drift.
  CHECKED: the gather's goals three ways (no slots, zero slots, the root target: the first root, every goal root,
  the first row's target, the later rows' zeros - all bitwise against the CPU's recipe); SEEN TO FAIL, 5 (the first
  root from the record after, the goal roots a block late, the target on the second row, a slot shifted, the first
  root from the table). The root's steps against the CPU's own chain, bitwise, and the policy reading each target
  after it is written (a goal root moved at decision 2 changes decision 2's action, not decision 1's); SEEN TO
  FAIL, 6 (the root from the same decision, the columns swapped, no spread, the slots over the state, twice the
  seconds, the root after the policy). ON THE DEVICE (lavapipe): the trainer fed two ways now also with the root
  target on - its parameters within the bar of the CPU-fed trainer's; SEEN TO FAIL with the device's root moved
  twice as fast (1111 epsilons, bar 64). The gather and rollout tests (7 + 8), the lab's refusal, the learner's root
  tests; the portable trainer builds (SPIR-V); lint, doc-gate, pages. A misplaced doc put back (`RowMask`).
  TUTORIAL: robot-mocap - "In the windows the policy trains on, the root is imagined" (the integration, the target,
  the circle worked).
  TIME, this turn: about 10 minutes of builds and tests (8 timed, the mutation runs beside).
  NEXT: I7 (4), the backward through the root - at each decision k >= 1 from the last down: the slots' gradient
  (`dp_at` past the goal's features) into the root's (`zm.poseSeenFromBackward`), carried with the later decisions'
  gradient, through `zm.integratePoseBackward` into state k's velocity columns (times the spread) and back to the root
  before; then I7 (5), the root's costs.

- Nov 19 (I7 (4), THIRD PART: the backward through the root - I7 (4) DONE). THE KERNEL (`lat_root_bwd`, one thread
  a row, at every decision k >= 1 from the last down, once the policy's input gradient at k and state k's other
  gradient parts are in): the gradient at root k - the one carried from the decisions after (a row's six numbers in

- Nov 19 (THE WINDOWS DRY RUN, and what it showed). The 1,362 MiB image started on the 5070 and ran the 20 minutes
  clean: 275 rounds of about 4 s (acting 2-3.5 s, training 0.2 s), no non-finite number, the judge at 15 minutes,
  stopped by itself. THE LEARNING DID NOT WORK: the judge's actor (the flow from its mode around the policy's average)
  lost the reference every 0.3-0.6 s at 15 minutes, where the servo alone lost it every 1.5-3.5 s; the bodies 9 cm
  off the reference instead of 2. Phase 1 (labels, 10 minutes, the gate never opened): the label loss ROSE (2e-4 to
  5e-2), the flow's distillation loss with it (3e-3 to 0.7). Phase 2: the world model's chained error from about 6 to
  thousands, the gate's world error to 10,680, the policy's gradient norm 1,000-16,000 before its clip at 20, the
  critic's tail (100-280) 10-30 times the tracking loss. Too many parts on at once to say which breaks it.
  FOUND: the console's "loses the reference every" was half the truth - the counts are decisions, read over the
  physics steps a second (fixed: decisions a second, as the status reads them); the device path never counts planned
  steps (`planned_step_share` 0 on the device - noted, not fixed).
  ADDED: the planners' own counts (`Resident.countPlannerDecision`, robotgpu_host's `countTrainerDecisions` given the
  planners now): `planner_steps_watched`, `planner_failures` in the log, "planners X s" on the console.
  THE LADDER (geno_ladder.zip, about 35 minutes on the 5070): 1 the teacher alone (the policy frozen, planners
  following every plan whole) - does the teacher beat the untrained policy; 2 plain SuperTrack - does the core learn;
  3 the teacher's labels alone (phase 1 held, no flow) - does copying the teacher help.

- Nov 19 (THE DRY RUN REVIEWED: what could break the learning, ranked). Read against the dry run's log, time.csv,
  kernel_times.csv and SuperMimic's own learners (`wm_learner.py`, `policy_learner.py`, `supermimic_runner.py`).
  1 THE LEARNER LEARNS FAR LESS PER RECORD THAN THE REFERENCE, IN FAR SMALLER BATCHES. The recipe's batch is 32
  windows; SuperMimic's world model takes 10 batches of 2,048 windows of 8 a call, its policy 4,096 rollouts of 32,
  paced so every collected transition is trained on 16 times (`replay_ratio`). Ours: 32 world updates of 32 windows a
  round of 16,384 records - each record trained on half a time, a tenth in phase 1, where 80% of the world model's
  batches are the candidates'. The world model's loss stayed flat for ten minutes (2.3 to 8.4 round to round, about 6);
  its state error fell from 0.70 to 0.31 of the no-change model's (bar 0.25), but its ANSWER TO AN ACTION never came:
  cosine 0.28-0.49 against the physics' (bar 0.8), length 0.15-0.26 of it (band 0.5-2) - an action's effect four
  times too weak, loosely aimed. Small batches are not cheaper on the device: a world update took 21 ms of GPU at 32
  rows (Muon's fixed iterations alone 12% of all GPU time), so larger batches cost far less than their size.
  2 PHASE 2 BEGAN AT ITS BOUND with that world model, every gate bar failed: the policy's rollouts, the critic's tail
  at the last state, the model planner's 40 characters all leaned on it, the rollouts left its data, and the gate's
  error rose to 10,680, the policy's gradient norm to 16,000.
  3 ABOUT 40% OF THE KEPT LABELS WERE A FALL's (fixed). A planner lives through an aftermath as every character does
  and replans there; `lost` is raised only at the loss's own decision, so stretches after it were kept. The dry run
  kept 200-300 labels a round of about 290 its planners labelled, while 40% of all records were after a loss.
  FIXED: `LabelBooks` drops a stretch with a decision after a loss (`stretch_after_loss`), counted apart
  (`labels_dropped_after_losses`, a new log column); teacher 2's examples follow, as they wait on the books.
  4 THE POLICY's CLIPS ARE NOT THE REFERENCE's: ours a length of 20, nothing per number; SuperMimic's a length of 1,
  then each number at 0.1, Adam's beta2 0.95 (ours too). Its rates 2e-4 for both networks; ours 1e-3 and 3e-4.
  5 THE WORLD MODEL's DATA IN PHASE 1: 80% candidates' lookaheads (whole-action plans drawn 0.3 rad about the last),
  the characters' windows from anywhere, 40% of them after a loss. SuperMimic's replay is its policy's own rollouts,
  ended at a termination.
  6 THE JUDGE at 15 minutes came after phase 2's breakdown (from 13.9 minutes): nothing measured the policy at the end
  of phase 1. It judges the flow's mode around the policy's average, not the policy alone.
  ALSO FIXED: the servo's baseline seconds (the trainer's own line) read decisions over physics steps a second - half
  the truth, as the console's was. Two tutorial folds still pointed at robot.zig for `normalizeQuat`,
  `rotateQuatByAngularVel` and `twoAxis`, moved to zimrmath (doc-folds failed on them).
  THE LADDER's RUN 4 (geno_ladder_4.zip): run 2's plain SuperTrack at about the reference's scale - 768 windows (the
  most this build holds with the horizon), both rates 2e-4, the policy's clips 1 and 0.1, a horizon of 16 decisions
  (0.53 s). The full system holds only 128 windows (its gradients' buffer at 99%); more needs the CPU twins' arenas out
  of the program's image (the 1.9 GB image would not start on Windows).
  PROPOSED for the next full run, once the ladder speaks: the batch as large as fits and more world updates a round;
  the reference's rates and clips; phase 2 opened by the gate alone; a judgement at phase 1's end; the candidates' share
  in phase 1 lowered.
  CHECKED: the label books' test with a fifth world living on after a loss (seen to fail with the drop disabled); the
  planners-following device test (labels: none dropped after losses, the scene's planners never lose); the lab's log
  tests; `--layout` at each batch; the desktop and Windows trainers; lint, doc-folds, doc-gate, the pages.

- Nov 19 (O7, FIRST PART: THE TRIPWIRES). SIMON: "C". A night of ten runs cannot afford one that learns nothing all
  night. BUILT, in the lab (`lab.Tripwire`, `TripwireReading`, `firstTripwire`, `TripwireBars`): seven tripwires in
  the order a learner is fed - replay_still, labels_absent, lookaheads_absent (planners asked for), weights_unmoved
  (a network due updates whose largest weight change is at most 1e-6), gradient_vanished (the world model's or the
  policy's latest length, where bounded), offsets_dead (no servo offset past 1e-6 rad), offsets_saturated (the median
  offset past a quarter turn). A NaN fails its bar. A network is due updates only once it can have them: the world
  model at every round, the policy after the world model's time alone, the critic and the flow once they have had
  their first (a flow learns only from examples). IN THE TRAINER: the first reading at the first round whose end has
  the weights back (every network's, the counts, the replay's head), the judgement `judged_after_rounds` (6) later,
  once; the servo's offsets read from the simulator's applied actions (the joints' offsets times the action's scale);
  the learner names its networks' ranges (`Resident.Network`, `networkParameters`). A miss ends the run
  (`RunState.failed_tripwire`, `RunStatus.tripwire`, exit 2, its state saved); when all hold the console says what
  each read. NOT READ: 4b's pairs.csv and the feasibility pass - neither exists in this trainer.
  CHECKED: the lab's tests - a healthy reading fires none, each miss fires its own in the table's order, a NaN fails,
